claims.text: Structural and chemical stability of multi-element, near-equiatomic nanoparticles at high temperature is governed by local atomic-scale short-range ordering.
Robust short-range order inhibits phase separation during heating.
Robust short-range order inhibits elemental segregation during heating.
Larger fluctuations in local ordering make nanoparticles more prone to instability.
The relevant as-synthesized nanoparticles initially contain a mixture of disordered and short-range-ordered atomic arrangements.
In situ high-temperature TEM with concurrent elemental mapping can monitor the evolution of local atomic ordering and segregation.
Enhanced short-range order minimizes local atomic fluctuations that lead to phase separation.
Enhanced short-range order minimizes local atomic fluctuations that lead to elemental segregation.
Short-range ordering raises the energy barrier against disorder-induced degradation at high temperature.
Nanoparticles retaining robust short-range order during heating will retain phase integrity better than the baseline.
Nanoparticles retaining robust short-range order during heating will retain a more homogeneous elemental distribution than the baseline.
Loss of local order or pronounced ordering fluctuations will be associated with increased elemental segregation, phase transitions, and chemical instability.
Nanoparticles processed without an intervention that promotes or preserves short-range order will undergo more local atomic fluctuations and high-temperature degradation.
The hypothesized relationship applies primarily to low-noble-metal-content, multi-element, near-equiatomic nanoparticles.
The influence of local ordering on stability may differ in systems with higher noble-metal content or different compositional tuning.

contradictions.description: The stated intervention is an observational characterization procedure, but the baseline is defined as lacking an intervention that promotes or preserves short-range order. No treatment that actually manipulates short-range order is specified, so the proposed comparison does not constitute the claimed controlled intervention and cannot cleanly separate ordering from compositional, size, synthesis, or thermal-history differences.
